titre: The Trial Where the Victim Is Tortured to Check Her Word
accroche: In 1612 in Rome, cords are tightened around Artemisia Gentileschi's fingers as she testifies. The man she accuses is never subjected to it.
contenu_vulgarise:
In 1612, a Roman court questions a nineteen-year-old woman about the details of a rape she says she suffered the year before. To verify that she is telling the truth, the judges have cords wound around her fingers, which a clerk tightens gradually as she answers questions. That device had a name in the procedure of the day: the *sibille*. The young woman is Artemisia Gentileschi; she will become one of the most renowned painters of the Italian Baroque. The accused is Agostino Tassi, an associate of her father, the painter Orazio Gentileschi, who filed the complaint.

## The Mechanism

The trial record, preserved in the State Archives of Rome, notes that Artemisia holds to her account during the torture, repeating that she is telling the truth as the cords tighten. The *sibille* is not a punishment: in Roman justice of the early 17th century, it is an accepted way of testing a witness's sincerity under pain, on a par with an oath. The trial, moreover, is less about the harm done to Artemisia than about the injury to the honor of the Gentileschi family, Tassi having promised her marriage before backing out, when he was already married elsewhere. During the hearing, the defense also tries to discredit the plaintiff by portraying her as depraved, and a midwife is summoned to examine her body.

Tassi, for his part, is never subjected to any comparable ordeal. He is nonetheless found guilty and sentenced to exile from Rome. That sentence is never carried out: he spends less than a year in prison and keeps working in the city in the years that follow.

## What It Shifts

The asymmetry is glaring: the accuser is tortured to verify her word, the accused is left untouched, and the penalty, when it comes, falls on no one. But the story does not end on that observation. A month after the trial, Artemisia's father arranges her marriage to a Florentine painter, and the family settles in Florence. Four years later, in 1616, Artemisia becomes the first woman admitted to the Accademia delle Arti del Disegno, the city's fine arts academy, at a time when women were excluded from such bodies almost everywhere.

The same judicial machinery that demanded proof of her sincerity under torture left her, in the immediate term, neither redress nor recognition. It was her work, in the years that followed, that would earn her both: paintings such as Judith Beheading Holofernes, painted after the trial, are read today by many art historians as a response to what she went through, though no document allows this to be stated with certainty.

repere.texte: The trial lasts seven months; Artemisia is nineteen when she undergoes the sibille during her testimony.

carte.punch: In 1612, Artemisia Gentileschi is tortured to check her word. The accused is never subjected to it.
carte.idee: During the rape trial she brings against Agostino Tassi, Artemisia Gentileschi has her fingers squeezed with cords to test the sincerity of her testimony. Tassi, the accused, is never subjected to it. He is convicted, but the sentence is never carried out.

quiz.question: Why is the sibille inflicted on Artemisia Gentileschi during the 1612 trial, and not on Agostino Tassi?
choix: Because the law of the day required systematically torturing the plaintiff in a rape trial
Because Tassi had already confessed to the acts and so no longer needed to be questioned
Because torture could legally be applied only to women in 17th-century Roman procedure
Because the sibille served to verify the sincerity of testimony, and it is she, not the accused, who testifies against him
quiz.explication: The sibille tested the truthfulness of testimony under pain; it applied to the person testifying, not the person accused, which explains the asymmetry without there having been any prior confession or any rule reserved for women.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to the text, what is the main issue in the 1612 trial, more than the harm done to Artemisia herself?
choix: The injury to the honor of the Gentileschi family
The theft of works belonging to Orazio Gentileschi
The breach of a commercial contract with Tassi
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text says the trial is less about the harm done to Artemisia than about the injury to the honor of the Gentileschi family.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What becomes of the exile sentence imposed on Agostino Tassi after his conviction?
choix: It is increased to life imprisonment
It is overturned by a Roman appeals court
It is never carried out: he keeps working in Rome
It is replaced by a fine paid to the Gentileschi family
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text specifies that the exile sentence is never carried out: Tassi spends less than a year in prison and keeps working in Rome.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What happens a month after the end of the trial, according to the text?
choix: Artemisia leaves on her own to settle in Rome
Her father arranges her marriage, and the family leaves for Florence
Tassi is permanently banished from Italy by the pope
Artemisia joins Tassi's studio as an apprentice
quiz_supplementaire.explication: A month after the trial, Artemisia's father arranges her marriage to a Florentine painter and the family settles in Florence.
